properties.name: "Nothing records why it was dropped" was said after reading only the requirement's own properties with get_node — the why was on the decision that retired it, one edge away, which get_node does not show
properties.source: this session's own error, corrected the same day
properties.statement:
INSTANCE, 2026-09-28, dev_reflow2 hub session. Linking a new requirement to req:context-is-a-modelled-quantity (status dropped), the agent read it with get_node, saw a statement that gave no reason, and wrote into two designs — and told Anthony — that the reason for the drop was unrecorded. It was recorded: dec:proposed-requirements-pruned (2026-07-30, on Anthony's word) retired it with an explicit reason, and the retired node is linked to it, as retire-from-design requires. The agent found it only after Anthony said he did not know, via git log -S on the committed export and then search_design for the decision.

THE LESSON, for the step it concerns: a node's STATUS says what happened to it; the decision that moved it says WHY, and that lives one edge away. get_node returns properties, not edges, so "the node does not say why" is a claim about one node's text, never about the design. Before saying a change's reason is unrecorded, read the node's connections (topic_report, or propagate_from depth 1) for a governing or retiring decision — which is what req:a-claim-that-the-design-holds-nothing-says-where-it-was-checked asks an absence claim to state. Three records were corrected the same day.
